label: GO step (choice time); magnitude largest after an unrewarded previous trial
explanation: Fires only at the GO step: on 88% of GO steps and never at D1 or D2. Within GO, the predicate is a phase marker and the information is in the magnitude. Magnitude is driven by the previous trial outcome: (GO & prev_reward==0) covers 99.8% of the top activation quartile but only about 6% of the bottom two quartiles (correlation 0.82 vs 0.70 for GO alone). Top windows show about 0.7-1.0 of max after unrewarded trials and about 0.1-0.4 after rewarded ones. It is silent or weak when the policy is indecisive (|choice| < 3) and in the last trials of the episode (ep_trial 90-99 rate 0.10), and also on the first trial of an episode. Adding ep_trial<85 raises precision to 0.95 but barely changes F1, so the simple GO predicate is recorded. All variables are observed (phase; prev_reward is shown at D1).

issues: The core claims hold. On dev the feature fires on 88.2% of GO steps and never at D1 or D2, and GO carries 100% of the activation mass. On test, phase==GO gives P 0.882, R 1.0, F1 0.937; misses on test show 0 missed activations. GO & prev_reward==0 gives P 0.969, corr 0.825 against 0.702 for GO alone, and covers 0.999 of the top quartile against about 0.06 of the bottom two. So the label (GO step, larger after an unrewarded trial) is supported.

One claim is false: 'weak or silent when the policy is undecided (|choice| < 3)'. On test, GO & -3<choice<3 has precision 0.80, close to the 0.88 base rate, and carries about 9% of the mass on about 7% of GO steps. The low rates for the middle choice bins in the profile (0.045 / 0.056) are taken over all phases, so D1 and D2 steps, where the feature never fires, dilute them. Gating on |choice| makes things worse: GO & |choice|>3 has F1 0.911 and GO & |choice|>2 has F1 0.921, both below 0.937.

One figure is misreported: 'rate 0.10 for ep_trial 90-99' is the rate over all phases. The GO-only rate for ep_trial>=90 is 0.32 on test (P 0.323). That is still a real, systematic drop from about 0.94 elsewhere, so the conclusion stands but the number overstates it by about 3x.
The first-trial claim holds: GO & ep_trial==0 has precision 0.013.

The remaining false positives are systematic but mild. They cluster at the first trial, the last ~10 trials, and GO steps after rewarded trials (GO & prev_reward==1: P 0.83; after an unrewarded trial: P 0.97). This is consistent with the stated magnitude story: weak activation after rewards sometimes drops to zero.

Slightly better observed-only predicate: (phase==GO)&(ep_trial>0)&(ep_trial<90), with test P 0.943, R 0.965, F1 0.954. That is a modest gain over 0.937, so the GO predicate is an acceptable simplification. No future variables are involved.
